subject: Camera image rotation and magnetometer mounting matrix, measured with the owner

cameras.method: Phone upright in portrait; one settled frame per camera (rear 820x616 binned viewfinder, front 1968x1200); owner confirmed scene facts (rear: window to the left of a bookshelf; front: an upright spray can). Frames viewed locally and deleted
cameras.result: Both cameras put the top of the scene on the image's left edge and need a 90 degree clockwise correction, with no mirroring (front label text reads normally after rotation). In DT/libcamera terms rotation = 270 for both; the original system's mount angles (rear 90, front 270) are Android clockwise corrections that agree
cameras.verified: r30: both sensor subdevices report camera_sensor_rotation 270; libcamera reports Rotation = 270

magnetometer.method: Six poses at a fixed heading (screen up/down, top up/down, right/left edge up), 60 samples each with the accelerometer confirming the pose. For each device axis the up-minus-down difference cancels the large hard-iron offset (about -2700 raw on z); the Earth's field points down here, so the raw axis that drops most when the device axis points up is that axis
magnetometer.open: hard-iron calibration (offsets about 8x the Earth field, likely the speaker magnet) belongs to userspace compass calibration
